The question asks for the probability that a student who likes green would dislike both colors, but Assistant A calculates the probability of a student who likes green disliking blue, which is not the same thing. Assistant B's answer to the second question is also incorrect, as it does not provide any calculations or reasoning to support the given probability.

The correct answer to the second question can be found using the conditional probability formula:

P(A' | B) = P(A' ∩ B) / P(B)

In this case, A' represents the event of disliking blue, B represents the event of liking green, and A' ∩ B represents the event of disliking blue and liking green.

P(A ∩ B) = 22% (probability of liking both colors)
P(B) = 45% (probability of liking green)
P(A' ∩ B) = P(B) - P(A ∩ B) = 45% - 22% = 23%

P(A' | B) = P(A' ∩ B) / P(B) = 23% / 45% ≈ 0.5111

So, the probability that a student who likes green would dislike blue is approximately 51.11%.
